is said that the most important thing a person can learn is how to read. Many of us, even adults, struggle with reading. In fact, reading difficulties, also called dyslexia, are quite common. According to the National Institutes of Health, as many as 1 in 10 children may be diagnosed with dyslexia.
Dyslexia is a learning disorder that makes reading difficult. It is not a sign of laziness, stupidity or lack of intelligence. It is not a disease or a mental disorder. People with dyslexia see letters and words differently than others. They may have trouble reading and writing, learning to read, understanding reading and writing, and speaking clearly.
Dyslexia is a disorder of the brain. It affects a person’s ability to read, spell, and write. A person with dyslexia may read words in reverse or read letters as whole words. They may have trouble with phonics or spelling.
Dyslexia can make it hard to remember things and understand directions. It can also cause problems with numbers, writing, and speaking clearly. People with dyslexia may have trouble with memory, attention, or language skills.
